questions.question: What were ‘privy purses’?

options.text: Pensions paid to the princes after integration

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pensions paid to the princes after integration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The privy purses were **annual payments made by the Government of India** to former princely rulers after the integration of princely states into independent India.
 
• The payments were part of an agreement during the integration process, ensuring **economic security to the princes** who surrendered their sovereignty.
 
• The privy purses were paid as compensation for **merging their states** into the Indian Union after independence in 1947.
 
• In 1971, the privy purses were **abolished** by the then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi through a constitutional amendment, citing reasons of equality and the need to end privileges.
 
• The abolition of privy purses marked a significant step in **eliminating feudal privileges** and ensuring a more egalitarian society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Integration of Princely States:**

 
 
• India had over **500 princely states** at the time of independence in 1947.
 
• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and V.P. Menon played a key role in integrating these states into the Indian Union.
 
• The princely rulers agreed to the merger in exchange for privileges, including privy purses.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Basis:**
 
 
• The privy purses were guaranteed under **Article 291 of the Indian Constitution**.
 
• They were later abolished through the **26th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1971**.
 
 
 
• **Reasons for Abolition:**
 
 
• The Indian government argued that privy purses were inconsistent with the **socialist and democratic ideals** of the Constitution.
 
• The move was seen as a step towards **ending hereditary privileges** and promoting equality.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Abolition:**
 
 
• The abolition of privy purses led to financial difficulties for some former rulers but was widely hailed as a progressive measure.
 
• It reinforced India's commitment to **egalitarianism and democratic values**.

questions.question: Which Hindustani music style has originated from the folk songs of the camel-riders of North-West India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tappa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Tappa** is a **semi-classical style of Hindustani music** that originated from the folk songs sung by camel riders in North-West India, particularly in Punjab.
 
• The word "**Tappa**" means "**jump**" or "**leap**," reflecting the fast, intricate, and rhythmic nature of this music style.
 
• Tappa is characterized by its highly ornamented and rapid musical phrases known as "**taan**" and "**gamak**."
 
• The style was popularized by **Ghulam Nabi Shori**, also known as "**Shori Miyan**," during the 18th century in the court of Nawab Asaf-ud-Daula of Awadh.
 
• Tappa compositions often express themes of love and longing and are performed in languages such as Punjabi and Urdu.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hindustani Classical Music:**

 
 
• Hindustani classical music is one of the two main traditions of Indian classical music, the other being Carnatic music.
 
• It originated in North India and is based on the system of "**ragas**" (melodic framework) and "**taals**" (rhythmic cycles).
 
• It incorporates elements of Persian and Mughal influences along with indigenous Indian traditions.
 
 
 
• **Other Hindustani Styles:**
 
 
• **Dhrupad:** The oldest style of Hindustani vocal music, characterized by its solemn and meditative nature.
 
• **Thumri:** A romantic and lyrical form of semi-classical music often associated with themes of love and devotion.
 
• **Khayal:** A more modern and improvisational style of Hindustani classical music that emphasizes creativity and emotional expression.
 
 
 
• **Gamak and Taan:**
 
 
• **Gamak:** Ornamentation in Indian classical music that involves oscillating or shaking notes.
 
• **Taan:** Fast, intricate melodic patterns that showcase the performer's virtuosity.
 
 
 
• **Regional Influence:**
 
 
• Tappa's roots lie in the folk traditions of camel riders from Punjab and North-West India.
 
• Its lyrics are often in regional languages, making it accessible and relatable to local audiences.

questions.question: Agro-forestry was conceived on the recommendation of which policy to promote plantation on farmlands?

options.text: Protection of Plant Varieties & Farmers' Rights Act, 2001

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Agro-forestry Policy, 2014**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **National Agro-forestry Policy, 2014** was introduced by the Government of India to promote agro-forestry practices across the country.
 
• This policy aims to integrate **trees and agriculture on farmland**, enhancing productivity, livelihoods, and environmental sustainability.
 
• The policy encourages farmers to grow trees alongside crops on their farmland, ensuring a balance between agricultural and forestry practices.
 
• It emphasizes the **relaxation of regulatory constraints** related to tree felling, transportation, and marketing of agro-forestry produce.
 
• The National Agro-forestry Policy, 2014, aligns with India's commitments to increasing forest cover and promoting sustainable agricultural practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agro-forestry:**

 
 
• Agro-forestry is a land-use system that integrates trees and shrubs with crops and livestock on the same land.
 
• It helps in improving **soil fertility, water retention, and biodiversity** while also providing economic benefits to farmers.
 
• Common agro-forestry practices include alley cropping, silvopasture, and windbreaks.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Agro-forestry:**
 
 
• It enhances carbon sequestration, contributing to climate change mitigation.
 
• Agro-forestry reduces soil erosion and improves soil health, ensuring sustainable farming practices.
 
• It provides additional income through timber, fruits, and other forest-based products.
 
 
 
• **National Forest Policy, 1988:**
 
 
• The National Forest Policy of 1988 emphasizes **maintaining ecological balance and preserving biodiversity**.
 
• The policy aims to** increase forest and tree cover to 33% of India's geographical area**.
 
 
 
• **India's Agro-forestry Mission:**
 
 
• The** National Agro-forestry Policy, 2014**, is implemented under the ambit of the **Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare**.
 
• It aligns with India's **National Action Plan on Climate Change** and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

questions.question: Under the reign of Islamic rulers, which among the following used to be a private building?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diwan-i-Khas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Diwan-i-Khas** was a private hall used by Islamic rulers, specifically for confidential meetings and royal audiences.
 
• It served as a venue where the emperor met his ministers, nobles, and other important officials to discuss state affairs privately.
 
• The design of Diwan-i-Khas reflected grandeur and exclusivity, symbolizing the ruler’s authority and status.
 
• Famous examples of Diwan-i-Khas can be found in Mughal architecture, such as the Red Fort in Delhi and Fatehpur Sikri.
 
• Unlike Diwan-i-Aam (Hall of Public Audience), which was open to the general public, Diwan-i-Khas was highly restricted and accessible only to select individuals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sarai**: Sarais were rest houses or inns constructed along trade routes to provide lodging and essential facilities to travelers, traders, and pilgrims.
 
• **Katra**: Katras were market complexes or caravanserais often used for commercial purposes. They were designed to accommodate traders and store goods.
 
• **Bridges**: Bridges constructed during the Islamic reign were primarily for public use, facilitating transportation and trade over rivers and other obstacles.
 
• **Diwan-i-Aam**: Unlike Diwan-i-Khas, the Diwan-i-Aam was a public hall where the emperor addressed grievances and petitions from common people.
 
• **Architectural Significance**: Structures like Diwan-i-Khas exemplify the blend of Persian, Islamic, and Indian architectural styles, showcasing intricate designs, inlaid marble work, and decorative arches.

questions.question: The Nizam of Hyderabad tried to project his rule as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a Muslim sovereignty in Deccan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Nizam of Hyderabad ruled one of the largest princely states in India, and his administration projected **Muslim sovereignty in the Deccan**, emphasizing Islamic traditions.
 
• The Nizam's dynasty traced its origins to the Mughal Empire and sought to maintain its **cultural and political identity** within the predominantly Hindu-majority region of the Deccan.
 
• The Nizam focused on **protecting and promoting Islamic culture** while maintaining a stable governance structure in his territory.
 
• Hyderabad became a hub for Islamic scholarship, architecture, and cultural preservation during the Nizam’s reign.
 
• Despite projecting Islamic sovereignty, the Nizam's administration included significant interactions with the British colonial powers to ensure political stability and economic trade benefits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hyderabad State:**

 
 
• Hyderabad was the largest princely state in India during British rule, covering areas of present-day Telangana, Karnataka, and Maharashtra.
 
• The state was ruled by the Nizam and known for its wealth, cultural diversity, and strategic importance.
 
 
 
• **Nizam's Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Nizam of Hyderabad belonged to the Asaf Jah dynasty, which was established in 1724.
 
• The dynasty maintained strong ties with the Mughal Empire and later with the British colonial rulers.
 
 
 
• **British Protectorate:**
 
 
• While the Nizam projected Islamic sovereignty, Hyderabad operated as a **British protectorate** under the subsidiary alliance system.
 
• The British provided military protection to the Nizam in exchange for control over the state's foreign affairs.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Contributions:**
 
 
• The Nizam's rule contributed to significant architectural landmarks like the Charminar and Mecca Masjid in Hyderabad.
 
• Hyderabad emerged as a center for Urdu literature, Islamic education, and cultural synthesis during this period.

questions.question: During the colonial period, India's industrial development was the result of British policies. Which of the following options best describes the nature of industrial development in India at the eve of independence?

options.text: Balanced regional distribution of heavy industries
Strong domestic capital goods industry in all provinces
Widespread industrial growth across rural and urban areas
Limited industrial activity, mainly concentrated in a few cities like Calcutta and Bombay

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Limited industrial activity, mainly concentrated in a few cities like Calcutta and Bombay**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• During the colonial period, India's industrial development was largely limited due to the exploitative economic policies of the British government.
 
• Industrial activity was mainly concentrated in a few urban centers like Bombay (now Mumbai), Calcutta (now Kolkata), and Madras (now Chennai).
 
• Heavy industries and large-scale manufacturing units were almost absent, with small-scale industries such as textiles and jute dominating the industrial landscape.
 
• India's domestic capital goods industry was virtually non-existent, forcing reliance on imports from Britain.
 
• The rural areas of India were primarily agrarian, with little to no industrial activity, leading to regional imbalances in economic development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Drain of Wealth Theory:** Proposed by Dadabhai Naoroji, it highlighted how colonial policies drained India's wealth to Britain, leaving limited resources for industrial development.
 
• **Deindustrialization:** The British systematically destroyed India's traditional handicrafts and small industries to promote British industrial goods, leading to widespread unemployment and poverty.
 
• **Economic Exploitation:** Colonial policies prioritized raw material exports (like cotton and jute) over domestic industrial growth, benefiting British industries at the expense of Indian economy.
 
• **Railways and Ports:** While infrastructure like railways and ports was developed, it primarily served colonial interests of transporting raw materials and finished goods rather than fostering industrial growth.
 
• **Post-Independence Scenario:** After independence, India focused on building a strong industrial base through initiatives like the Five-Year Plans and establishment of public sector enterprises.

questions.question: Which of the following modern physicist closely examined Newtonian mechanics’ foundations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Albert Einstein**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Albert Einstein critically examined the foundations of Newtonian mechanics and introduced revolutionary concepts that led to the development of modern physics.
 
• His theory of special relativity (1905) challenged Newtonian mechanics by introducing the constancy of the speed of light and the relativity of simultaneity.
 
• Einstein’s work revealed that Newtonian mechanics fails at speeds approaching the speed of light and in strong gravitational fields, leading to the development of general relativity (1915).
 
• The equivalence principle, a cornerstone of general relativity, contradicted Newton’s concept of absolute space and time.
 
• Einstein’s contributions fundamentally reshaped the understanding of space, time, and energy, pushing science beyond the classical framework established by Newton.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newtonian Mechanics:**

 
 
• A classical physics framework developed by Sir Isaac Newton, describing motion using laws of inertia, force, and action-reaction.
 
• It assumes absolute space and time, which Einstein later challenged.
 
 
 
• **Special Relativity:**
 
 
• Developed by Albert Einstein in 1905, it introduced concepts like time dilation, length contraction, and E=mc².
 
• It applies to objects moving at constant speeds close to the speed of light.
 
 
 
• **General Relativity:**
 
 
• Published by Einstein in 1915, it describes gravity as the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy.
 
• It replaced Newton’s law of universal gravitation in explaining phenomena like black holes and cosmic expansion.
 
 
 
• **Equivalence Principle:**
 
 
• A concept in general relativity stating that gravitational force and acceleration are indistinguishable.
 
• It played a key role in Einstein’s departure from Newtonian mechanics.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Modern Physics:**
 
 
• Einstein’s work laid the foundation for quantum mechanics, cosmology, and advancements in theoretical physics.
 
• His discoveries opened new avenues in understanding the universe at both macroscopic and microscopic scales.

questions.question: How many major ragas are there in Carnatic music?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**72**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In Carnatic music, there are **72 Melakarta ragas**, which are also called parent or fundamental ragas.
 
• The Melakarta system is a **comprehensive framework** for classifying all possible ragas based on specific scales.
 
• Each Melakarta raga consists of **seven swaras (notes)**: Sa, Ri, Ga, Ma, Pa, Da, Ni, in ascending (Arohana) and descending (Avarohana) order.
 
• The 72 Melakarta ragas are divided into **12 chakras (groups)**, each containing six ragas.
 
• These Melakarta ragas serve as a foundation for deriving **Janya ragas**, which are more specific and commonly used in compositions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Melakarta Ragas:**

 
 
• Each Melakarta raga must have all seven swaras (notes) in both ascending (Arohana) and descending (Avarohana) scales.
 
• They strictly follow the rules of Carnatic music theory, such as having a fixed set of intervals between notes.
 
 
 
• **Chakras in Melakarta System:**
 
 
• The 72 Melakarta ragas are grouped into 12 chakras (sets), each named after a specific concept (e.g., Indu, Netra, Agni).
 
• Each chakra contains six Melakarta ragas, differentiated by variations in the Ri, Ga, Da, and Ni swaras.
 
 
 
• **Janya Ragas:**
 
 
• Janya ragas are derived from Melakarta ragas and may include fewer than seven swaras or employ irregular note patterns.
 
• They are more commonly used in Carnatic compositions and improvisations.
 
 
 
• **Swaras in Carnatic Music:**
 
 
• The seven basic swaras are: Shadja (Sa), Rishabha (Ri), Gandhara (Ga), Madhyama (Ma), Panchama (Pa), Dhaivata (Da), and Nishada (Ni).
 
• Each swara has variants (e.g., Shuddha, Chatushruti, Antara) that define the raga's scale.

questions.question: Where is the Indian naval air station INS Baaz located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Great Nicobar Island**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• INS Baaz is located on the **Great Nicobar Island**, which is the southernmost island of the Andaman and Nicobar archipelago.
 
• It was commissioned on **31st July 2012** as a naval air station to enhance surveillance and operational capabilities in the Indian Ocean Region (IOR).
 
• The station is strategically located near the **Six Degree Channel**, a vital sea lane through which significant global trade passes.
 
• INS Baaz is pivotal for India’s **maritime security** and helps monitor the movement of ships and submarines in the region.
 
• The air station supports operations of aircraft such as the Dornier and helicopters, and it is capable of enabling future expansion for larger aircraft.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**

 
 
• The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are a group of 572 islands located in the Bay of Bengal.
 
• They serve as India’s easternmost boundary and are of strategic importance for maritime trade and security.
 
• The islands act as a natural outpost for monitoring the **Malacca Strait**, one of the world's busiest shipping lanes.
 
 
 
• **Six Degree Channel**
 
 
• It is also known as the Great Channel and lies between the Great Nicobar Island and the Indonesian island of Sumatra.
 
• This channel is approximately 10 degrees north of the equator and is a crucial shipping route connecting the Indian Ocean to the Pacific Ocean.
 
 
 
• **Indian Naval Air Stations**
 
 
• Indian Naval Air Stations provide logistical and operational support for the Indian Navy’s air assets.
 
• Other key air stations include INS Hansa in Goa and INS Rajali in Tamil Nadu.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance of INS Baaz**
 
 
• The station enhances India’s ability to secure its Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) and monitor the **Indo-Pacific region**.
 
• It plays a key role in disaster relief operations, search and rescue missions, and maritime domain awareness.

questions.question: 'Vilambit' and 'Drut' are two varieties of which of the following singing styles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Khayal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Khayal** is a prominent form of Indian classical music that emphasizes improvisation and melody, showcasing a blend of creativity and technicality.
 
• The terms **Vilambit** (slow tempo) and **Drut** (fast tempo) are specific to Khayal and refer to the tempo of the composition being performed.
 
• In Khayal singing, the artist typically begins with a Vilambit rendition to explore the raga in depth, followed by a Drut composition to exhibit technical virtuosity.
 
• Khayal originated in the 13th century but gained prominence during the Mughal era, especially under the patronage of rulers like Muhammad Shah Rangile.
 
• It is characterized by its poetic lyrics (often depicting themes of love or devotion) and its ability to provide extensive room for improvisation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vilambit and Drut:**

 
 
• Vilambit refers to the slow-paced rendition of a Khayal composition, allowing detailed exploration of the raga.
 
• Drut refers to the fast-paced section, which is typically performed after the Vilambit and highlights rhythmic complexity and speed.
 
 
 
• **Structure of Khayal:**
 
 
• Each Khayal performance comprises two sections: **Asthai** (the initial refrain) and **Antara** (the subsequent verse).
 
• The artist improvises on both sections while adhering to the rules of the raga.
 
 
 
• **Other Classical Styles:**
 
 
• **Dhrupad:** An ancient and highly structured form of classical music focusing on devotional themes.
 
• **Thumri:** A semi-classical style known for its romantic and expressive nature.
 
• **Tappa:** A semi-classical genre characterized by its intricate and fast-paced melodic patterns.
 
 
 
• **Modern Relevance:**
 
 
• Khayal continues to be a significant part of Indian classical music, performed by eminent artists in concerts and festivals worldwide.
 
• Leading gharanas (schools) like Gwalior, Kirana, and Agra have contributed to its evolution and diversity.

questions.question: Paika is the famous folk dance of which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jharkhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Paika** is a traditional folk dance form originating from the state of **Jharkhand**.
 
• This dance is performed by the Paika community, who were historically associated with martial traditions.
 
• The performers use swords and shields, showcasing their combat skills through synchronized and energetic movements.
 
• Paika dance is often performed during festivals and community gatherings, symbolizing valor and the warrior spirit.
 
• The dance is accompanied by traditional musical instruments like the **Mandar** and **Shehnai**, adding rhythm and vibrancy to the performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Folk Dance:** Folk dances are traditional performances that reflect the cultural heritage, history, and lifestyle of a specific community or region.
 
• **Jharkhand:** Known as the "Land of Forests," this state in eastern India is rich in tribal culture and traditions, with numerous folk dances like Chhau, Jhumar, and Paika.
 
• **Paika Community:** The Paika were historically a warrior class in Jharkhand, serving as foot soldiers or militia in ancient and medieval times.
 
• **Chhau Dance:** Another famous folk dance of Jharkhand, Chhau is a semi-classical dance form with martial, tribal, and folk origins, often performed with masks.
 
• **Preservation of Folk Art:** Efforts are being made by the Indian government and cultural organizations to preserve and promote traditional folk dances like Paika through festivals, workshops, and documentation.

questions.question: Which of the following dance forms is often accompanied by the famous song form 'Thumri'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kathak** is one of the eight classical dance forms of India and is known for its intricate footwork, spins, and expressive gestures.
 
• The dance form is closely associated with the Hindustani classical music tradition, and **'Thumri'** is one of the primary song forms used as an accompaniment.
 
• 'Thumri' is a semi-classical vocal genre characterized by its romantic or devotional themes and is often rendered in a light and emotive style.
 
• Kathak performances often involve storytelling through dance, and the expressive nature of 'Thumri' complements the abhinaya (expressive) aspect of the dance.
 
• The use of 'Thumri' in Kathak highlights the synergy between the dance and music traditions of North India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thumri:**

 
 
• A semi-classical form of Hindustani vocal music, known for its lyrical and emotive content.
 
• It is primarily based on themes of love, separation, and devotion, often focusing on Radha-Krishna narratives.
 
• Thumri compositions are often performed in lighter ragas and have a flexible, improvisational structure.
 
 
 
• **Abhinaya in Kathak:**
 
 
• Refers to the expressive aspect of Kathak, where the dancer conveys emotions and narratives through facial expressions, hand gestures, and body movements.
 
• 'Thumri' enhances the abhinaya element by providing a musical backdrop rich in emotion and lyrical beauty.
 
 
 
• **Kathak's Historical Roots:**
 
 
• Originated in the temples of North India as a storytelling art form where dancers narrated mythological tales.
 
• Later, it was influenced by Mughal culture, adding elements of courtly entertainment and Persian artistry.
 
 
 
• **Other Classical Dance Forms of India:**
 
 
• Some of the other prominent classical dance forms include Bharatanatyam, Odissi, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Kathakali, and Sattriya.
 
• Each has its unique music, style, and cultural significance tied to the region of its origin.

questions.question: The tripartite struggle for Kannauj was among the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Palas, Gurjara-Pratiharas and Rashtrakutas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The tripartite struggle for Kannauj was a power struggle between three major dynasties: **Palas, Gurjara-Pratiharas, and Rashtrakutas**.
 
• Kannauj, located in present-day Uttar Pradesh, was a strategically significant city due to its location on the Ganga trade route and its historical importance.
 
• The struggle began in the 8th century and continued into the 9th century, as each dynasty sought to control Kannauj to assert dominance over Northern India.
 
• The Gurjara-Pratiharas, under rulers such as Nagabhata I and Mihira Bhoja, played a key role in the struggle by frequently contesting the Palas and Rashtrakutas.
 
• The Rashtrakutas, led by rulers like Dhruva Dharavarsha and Govinda III, launched northern expeditions to claim Kannauj, intensifying the conflict.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pala Dynasty:**

 
 
• Founded by Gopala in the 8th century, the Pala Empire was known for its patronage of Buddhism and significant contributions to art and education.
 
• The Palas ruled over Bengal and Bihar, with Dharampala and Devapala being prominent rulers during the tripartite struggle.
 
 
 
• **Gurjara-Pratihara Dynasty:**
 
 
• This dynasty emerged in western and northern India, with its capital shifting to Kannauj during its peak.
 
• Known for its resistance to Arab invasions, the Pratiharas played a significant role in preserving Indian culture during this era.
 
 
 
• **Rashtrakuta Dynasty:**
 
 
• Originating from the Deccan region, the Rashtrakutas were known for their military prowess and cultural achievements, such as the construction of the Kailasanatha Temple at Ellora.
 
• Their rulers often launched northern campaigns, bringing them into conflict with the Palas and Pratiharas.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance of Kannauj:**
 
 
• Kannauj was a key center of trade, administration, and cultural exchange in medieval India.
 
• Control over Kannauj symbolized political supremacy over Northern India, making it a coveted prize for the rival dynasties.

questions.question: In which type of musical instruments is sound produced by blowing air into a hollow column?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sushira Vadya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sushira Vadya** refers to wind instruments where sound is produced by blowing air into a hollow column.
 
• Common examples of Sushira Vadya include the flute, shehnai, and harmonium.
 
• The vibration of air within the hollow tube creates sound, and the pitch can be varied by changing the length of the air column.
 
• These instruments are categorized under the ancient Indian classification of musical instruments based on how sound is produced.
 
• Sushira Vadya is distinct from other categories like Tata Vadya (string instruments) or Avanaddha Vadya (percussion instruments).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Classification of Indian Musical Instruments:**

 
 
• Indian instruments are traditionally classified into four types: Tata Vadya (string instruments), Avanaddha Vadya (percussion instruments), Sushira Vadya (wind instruments), and Ghana Vadya (solid instruments).
 
 
 
• **Mechanism of Sound Production:**
 
 
• In Sushira Vadya, air vibrations caused by blowing into the instrument generate sound waves within the hollow column.
 
• The frequency of these waves determines the pitch, which can be manipulated using finger holes or valves.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Sushira Vadya:**
 
 
• Traditional instruments: Flute, Shehnai, Nadaswaram.
 
• Modern instruments: Clarinet, Saxophone.
 
 
 
• **Role in Indian Music:**
 
 
• Sushira Vadya plays a vital role in both classical and folk music traditions.
 
• These instruments are often used for melody and accompaniment.

questions.question: Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve spans which of the following groups of Indian states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve is India's first biosphere reserve, established in **1986**.
 
• It spans across three Indian states: **Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka**.
 
• The reserve covers an area of approximately **5,520 square kilometers**.
 
• It is part of the **Western Ghats**, a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for its rich biodiversity.
 
• The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve is home to several endemic species, including the **Nilgiri Tahr** and the **Lion-tailed Macaque**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biosphere Reserve:**

 
 
• A biosphere reserve is an area designated to protect biodiversity and promote sustainable development.
 
• It comprises three zones: the core area (protected region), buffer zone (activities promoting conservation), and transition area (sustainable resource use).
 
 
 
• **Western Ghats:**
 
 
• The Western Ghats is one of the eight "hottest hotspots" of biological diversity in the world.
 
• It is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its unique ecosystems.
 
 
 
• **Flora and Fauna:**
 
 
• The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve hosts over **3,000 species of flowering plants** and a variety of mammals, birds, reptiles, and insects.
 
• Endangered species like the **Tiger**, **Elephant**, and **Nilgiri Langur** are found here.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO Program:**
 
 
• The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve is part of UNESCO’s **Man and Biosphere (MAB) Program**, which promotes conservation and sustainable development.
 
• It aims to balance environmental conservation with human activity.

questions.question: The endangered bird species found in the Thar Desert is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Great Indian Bustard**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Great Indian Bustard** is one of the heaviest flying birds, primarily found in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• It is critically endangered and has been listed in the **IUCN Red List** due to its rapidly declining population.
 
• The bird is native to arid and semi-arid regions, especially the **Thar Desert** in Rajasthan, which serves as its primary habitat.
 
• Major threats include **habitat loss**, poaching, and collisions with power lines.
 
• Conservation efforts include the **Great Indian Bustard Conservation Program** and the establishment of wildlife sanctuaries like the **Desert National Park**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thar Desert:**

 
 
• The Thar Desert, also known as the Great Indian Desert, is located in northwestern India and eastern Pakistan.
 
• It is characterized by extreme temperatures, low rainfall, and sandy terrain, making it one of the most arid regions in India.
 
 
 
• **Critically Endangered Species:**
 
 
• Species listed as "Critically Endangered" by the **IUCN Red List** face an extremely high risk of extinction in the wild.
 
• Examples include the Great Indian Bustard, Vaquita, and Axolotl.
 
 
 
• **Desert National Park:**
 
 
• Located in Rajasthan, this park is one of the largest wildlife sanctuaries in India and a key habitat for the Great Indian Bustard.
 
• The park also supports other species like desert foxes, eagles, and sand grouse.
 
 
 
• **Conservation Challenges:**
 
 
• The Great Indian Bustard faces threats such as habitat fragmentation, hunting, and infrastructure development.
 
• Innovative solutions like the installation of bird diverters on power lines are being implemented to prevent collisions.

questions.question: Which of the following classical dance forms' music belongs to the Carnatic system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuchipudi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kuchipudi** is a classical dance form originating from Andhra Pradesh, India.
 
• The music accompanying Kuchipudi performances is based on the **Carnatic system**, one of the two main traditions of Indian classical music.
 
• Kuchipudi performances often feature **vocals and instrumental accompaniments** typical of Carnatic music, such as veena, mridangam, and flute.
 
• The dance form combines **rhythmic footwork** with expressive storytelling through gestures, known as "abhinaya."
 
• Kuchipudi is known for its fusion of **dance, drama, and music**, all rooted in the rich Carnatic tradition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carnatic Music:**

 
 
• Carnatic music is primarily associated with the southern states of India: Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Kerala.
 
• It is characterized by its complex **raga (melody)** and **tala (rhythm)** systems.
 
• Famous composers like **Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar**, and **Shyama Shastri** have contributed significantly to its repertoire.
 
 
 
• **Other Classical Dance Forms:**
 
 
• **Odissi:** Originating from Odisha, it primarily uses Hindustani music.
 
• **Kathak:** Associated with North India, it uses Hindustani music and focuses on intricate footwork and spins.
 
• **Chhau:** A semi-classical dance form popular in eastern India, it uses regional folk music styles.
 
 
 
• **Key Instruments in Carnatic Music:**
 
 
• Veena, mridangam, violin, and tambura are commonly used.
 
• These instruments create a rich soundscape that complements the dance performance.
 
 
 
• **Abhinaya in Kuchipudi:**
 
 
• Abhinaya refers to expressive storytelling through gestures, facial expressions, and body movements.
 
• Kuchipudi often incorporates mythological and spiritual narratives in its performances.

questions.question: Which of the following materials has been mainly used for building the Jahangiri Mahal in Agra Fort?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Red sandstone**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Jahangiri Mahal** is one of the most significant structures inside the **Agra Fort**, which is a UNESCO World Heritage site located in **Agra, Uttar Pradesh, India**.
 
• This architectural marvel was primarily constructed using **red sandstone**, a material commonly used in Mughal architecture during the medieval period.
 
• **Red sandstone** was chosen for its **durability, strength, and aesthetic appeal**. It also provided the structure with a distinctive reddish hue, which is iconic to Mughal buildings.
 
• The use of **red sandstone** reflects the Mughal preference for combining **functional durability** with **artistic elegance**.
 
• The Jahangiri Mahal served as a **residential palace** for the royal women, particularly the wives of Emperor Akbar and other Mughal queens.
 
• The intricate carvings and designs on the red sandstone highlight the **artistic advancements** of the Mughal era and their expertise in architectural detailing.
 
• The Agra Fort itself, including the Jahangiri Mahal, was commissioned by **Emperor Akbar** in the 16th century as a symbol of the Mughal Empire's grandeur.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Concrete**__

 __
 
• **Concrete** is a modern construction material made from a mixture of **cement, sand, gravel, and water**.
 
• It was not available during the Mughal era, making it historically inaccurate as a material for the Jahangiri Mahal.
 
• Concrete is widely used in modern-day constructions for its **strength and versatility**.
 
 
 
• **White marble**__
 __
 
• **White marble** was another material prominently used during the Mughal period, especially in structures like the **Taj Mahal**.
 
• However, white marble was used more for structures emphasizing **grandeur and purity**, while red sandstone was preferred for **forts and palaces**.
 
 
 
• **Ceramic**__
 
 
• **Ceramic** refers to materials made from clay that are hardened by heat.
 
• This material is more suited for **decorative tiles, pottery, or small-scale architectural features**, not large-scale buildings like the Jahangiri Mahal.

questions.question: Which of the following is a 'Tata Vadya'?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Veena**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Tata Vadya** refers to a class of musical instruments in Indian classical music where the sound is produced by the vibration of strings.
 
• The **Veena** is one of the most ancient and revered Indian string instruments, classified as a **melodic Tata Vadya.**
 
• The Veena is used extensively in both **Carnatic and Hindustani classical music.**
 
• It has a long, fretted neck and a resonator made of wood, with strings that are plucked to produce sound.
 
• The Veena is traditionally associated with **Saraswati, the Hindu goddess of wisdom and music.**
 
• Different types of Veena include **Rudra Veena, Saraswati Veena, and Chitra Veena,** each catering to various styles and regions.
 
• It plays a vital role in Indian music as it produces a rich and melodious sound, making it a cornerstone instrument in classical performances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bansuri**__

 __
 
• The **Bansuri** is a wind instrument and does not belong to the **Tata Vadya** category.
 
• It is a traditional Indian bamboo flute associated with **Lord Krishna** and is widely used in **Hindustani classical music.**
 
• The Bansuri produces sound by blowing air across the hole and manipulating finger positions to create different notes.
 
 
 
• **Dhol**__
 __
 
• The **Dhol** is a percussion instrument and falls under the category of **Avanaddha Vadya** (membranous instruments).
 
• It is prominently used in **folk and traditional music** across various regions of India.
 
• The Dhol is played by striking its surface with sticks or hands, producing rhythmic beats.
 
 
 
• **Manjira**__
 
 
• The **Manjira** is a type of **Idiophone**, which produces sound through vibrations of the instrument itself.
 
• It is a small, hand-held cymbal used in **devotional and folk music.**
 
• The instrument is played by striking two cymbals together to create a rhythmic clinking sound.

questions.question: The NK Singh Committee, which was formed in 2016, was associated with which of the following?

options.text: Reviewing the trade deficit in India

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Reviewing the FRBM Act, 2003**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **NK Singh Committee** was set up in **2016** to review the provisions of the **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2003**.
 
• The **FRBM Act, 2003**, was enacted by the Indian Government to ensure **fiscal discipline** and reduce fiscal deficits.
 
• The Committee, chaired by **NK Singh**, aimed to make recommendations on revising the fiscal roadmap in light of **changing macroeconomic conditions**.
 
• It proposed introducing a new framework for fiscal policy, focusing on **debt and deficit targets**, and recommended specific **escape clauses** for unforeseen situations like natural disasters or economic crises.
 
• The Committee suggested setting a target for the **government’s debt-to-GDP ratio** and recommended measures for better **transparency and accountability** in fiscal management.
 
• It emphasized the importance of fiscal discipline for **economic stability** and long-term growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Introduction of Standing Deposit Facility**__

 __
 
• The **Standing Deposit Facility (SDF)** is a monetary tool introduced by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** to manage liquidity in the banking system.
 
• The SDF allows the RBI to absorb excess funds from banks without requiring the collateral that is typically needed in open market operations.
 
• The SDF was not related to the NK Singh Committee but was part of broader measures in monetary policy frameworks.
 
 
 
• **Reviewing the trade deficit in India**__
 __
 
• The term **trade deficit** refers to a situation where a country's imports exceed its exports.
 
• Trade deficit reviews are generally conducted by the **Ministry of Commerce** or related economic bodies, not by the NK Singh Committee.
 
 
 
• **Introduction of Monetary Policy Committee**__
 
 
• The **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** was established in **2016** under the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**, to set the policy interest rates.
 
• The MPC is composed of six members, including three from the RBI and three external experts appointed by the Government of India.
 
• This was a separate initiative and not related to the NK Singh Committee.

questions.question: The Digital India initiative, launched in 2015, marked a significant step in India’s postreform development trajectory. Which of the following is NOT a pillar of the Digital India initiative?

options.text: Digital Infrastructure as a Utility to Every Citizen

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Privatisation of Internet Services**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Digital India initiative**, launched in **2015**, aims to transform India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy.
 
• The initiative is based on three core pillars:
 
 
• **Digital Infrastructure as a Utility to Every Citizen**: Ensures high-speed internet access, mobile connectivity, and digital identity for all citizens.
 
• **Governance and Services on Demand**: Focuses on integrating government services digitally to ensure real-time availability and transparency.
 
• **Digital Empowerment of Citizens**: Aims to make citizens digitally literate and empower them to access digital services.
 
 
 
• **Privatisation of Internet Services** is NOT a pillar of the Digital India initiative. The initiative focuses on making internet services accessible and affordable to all citizens, rather than privatizing them.
 
• The Digital India initiative emphasizes inclusivity and affordability, ensuring universal access to technology without promoting privatization.
 
• The correct answer highlights the distinction between the core principles of the initiative and unrelated concepts like privatization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Governance and Services on Demand**__

 __
 
• Focuses on the **real-time availability** of government services.
 
• Includes **e-Governance platforms** to enhance accessibility and transparency.
 
• Examples include platforms like **DigiLocker** and **UMANG**.
 
 
 
• **Digital Infrastructure as a Utility to Every Citizen**__
 __
 
• Aims to provide **universal internet access** and **digital identity** to citizens.
 
• Includes initiatives like **Aadhaar** and **BharatNet** for robust digital infrastructure.
 
• Ensures **cybersecurity measures** to protect citizen data.
 
 
 
• **Digital Empowerment of Citizens**__
 
 
• Focuses on improving **digital literacy** among citizens.
 
• Promotes the availability of **local language content** and **digital platforms**.
 
• Empowers citizens to **participate in the digital economy**.

questions.question: A UNESCO World Heritage Site, the Kakatiya Rudreshwara Temple is situated in which of the following states of India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Telangana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kakatiya Rudreshwara Temple**, also known as the **Ramappa Temple**, is located in **Palampet village**, in the **Mulugu district** of **Telangana**.
 
• The temple was built during the reign of the **Kakatiya dynasty** in the **13th century**.
 
• This temple is dedicated to **Lord Shiva** and is renowned for its **intricate carvings** and exceptional architectural style.
 
• The Ramappa Temple is notable for its usage of **lightweight bricks**, known as **floating bricks**, which were used in the construction of the roof.
 
• In **2021**, the temple was inscribed as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**, making it the first heritage site from Telangana to receive this recognition.
 
• The temple serves as an outstanding example of **Kakatiya art and architecture**, showcasing the cultural and historical legacy of the region.
 
• It attracts visitors and scholars from around the world due to its **historical significance** and **unique craftsmanship.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Karnataka**__

 __
 
• Karnataka is home to several UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including **Hampi**, which was the capital of the **Vijayanagara Empire**.
 
• Hampi is famous for its **monolithic sculptures** and **architectural ruins**.
 
• The state also features other renowned heritage sites such as **Pattadakal**, known for its **Chalukya-style temples**.
 
 
 
• **Andhra Pradesh**__
 __
 
• Andhra Pradesh is known for its historical landmarks such as the **Amaravati Stupa**, which is an important Buddhist site.
 
• The **Lepakshi Temple**, famous for its **hanging pillar**, is another architectural marvel in the state.
 
• However, the Kakatiya Rudreshwara Temple is not located in Andhra Pradesh but in Telangana, which was carved out as a separate state in **2014**.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat**__
 
 
• Gujarat has several UNESCO World Heritage Sites, such as the **Rani ki Vav**, an intricately designed stepwell located in Patan.
 
• The **Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park**, featuring ancient forts and temples, is another recognized site in Gujarat.
 
• The state is also famous for its **Gir National Park**, the last abode of the Asiatic lions.

questions.question: The easternmost extension of the Himalayas does NOT include which of the following?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Khasi Hills**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Khasi Hills** are located in the northeastern state of **Meghalaya**, India.
 
• They are part of the **Meghalaya Plateau**, which is distinct from the Himalayas.
 
• The Khasi Hills consist of rolling hills and are well-known for their **lush green landscapes** and **rich biodiversity**.
 
• This region is famous for its **living root bridges**, an example of traditional ecological engineering.
 
• The Khasi Hills are primarily inhabited by the **Khasi tribal community**, who have a unique culture and language.
 
• Unlike the Naga, Patkai, and Mizo Hills, which are considered extensions of the eastern Himalayas, the Khasi Hills belong to the **Peninsular Block** and are geologically older.
 
• They do not share the tectonic or geographical characteristics associated with the Himalayan range.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Naga Hills**__

 __
 
• The **Naga Hills** are located in the northeastern states of **Nagaland** and **Manipur**.
 
• They form part of the **Arakan Yoma range**, which is considered an eastern extension of the Himalayas.
 
• The Naga Hills are known for their **rugged terrain** and dense forests.
 
• This region is inhabited by the **Naga tribes**, who have a rich cultural heritage.
 
 
 
• **Patkai Hills**__
 __
 
• The **Patkai Hills**, also known as the **Patkai Bum**, are located along the northeastern border of India, including parts of **Arunachal Pradesh** and **Nagaland**.
 
• They are part of the **Himalayan mountain system** and are known for their high rainfall and dense vegetation.
 
• The Patkai Hills act as a natural barrier between India and Myanmar.
 
 
 
• **Mizo Hills**__
 
 
• The **Mizo Hills**, also known as the **Lushai Hills**, are located in the northeastern state of **Mizoram**.
 
• They are considered part of the **easternmost extension of the Himalayas**.
 
• This region is known for its **undulating hills** and **rich flora and fauna**.
 
• The Mizo Hills are primarily inhabited by the **Mizo tribes**.

questions.question: Which group of islands lies between 8° – 12° 13″ North latitude and 71° – 74° East longitude?

__
 
• The **Lakshadweep Islands** are a group of **36 small islands** located in the Arabian Sea off the southwestern coast of India.
 
• These islands lie between the latitude of **8° – 12° 13′ North** and the longitude of **71° – 74° East**.
 
• The Lakshadweep archipelago includes **12 atolls, 3 reefs, and 5 submerged banks**.
 
• It is India's **smallest Union Territory** and is known for its **pristine beaches, coral reefs, and rich marine biodiversity**.
 
• The capital of Lakshadweep is **Kavaratti**, which is also the largest city in the region.
 
• The islands are famous for their **tourism, fishing, and coconut cultivation**.
 
• Being of **strategic importance**, the Lakshadweep Islands also play a key role in India's maritime security.
 
• These islands are formed from **coral deposits** and are known for their ecological significance and beauty.

 __

questions.question: What is the name of the pillared hall at the front of a Hindu temple where devotees gather?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mandapa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Mandapa** is the pillared hall in front of the sanctum of a Hindu temple where devotees gather for prayers or rituals.
 
• It serves as a transitional space between the outer world and the sanctum (Garbhagriha) of the temple.
 
• Mandapas can be used for various religious and cultural activities, including congregations, dances, and discourses.
 
• Architecturally, the Mandapa is often ornately decorated with carvings and sculptures depicting mythological stories or deities.
 
• In larger temples, there may be multiple Mandapas, each serving a specific purpose, such as the Ardha-Mandapa (entrance porch) and Maha-Mandapa (great hall).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Garbhagriha:**

 
 
• The sanctum sanctorum of a Hindu temple where the main deity resides.
 
• It is the most sacred and innermost part of the temple.
 
• Access to the Garbhagriha is often restricted to priests or devotees during specific ceremonies.
 
 
 
• **Amalaka:**
 
 
• A stone disc, often ribbed, placed atop the temple shikhara (tower).
 
• It symbolizes the sun and is considered an important architectural and spiritual element in temple design.
 
 
 
• **Antarala:**
 
 
• A vestibule or intermediary space between the Garbhagriha and the Mandapa.
 
• It serves as a transitional area and provides visual as well as spiritual separation between the sanctum and the outer hall.
 
 
 
• **Temple Architecture:**
 
 
• Hindu temples are broadly categorized into Nagara (North Indian), Dravida (South Indian), and Vesara (mixed) styles.
 
• Each style has unique features, such as the shikhara in Nagara style and the gopuram in Dravida style.
 
 
 
• **Role of Mandapa in Rituals:**
 
 
• The Mandapa is often used for Vedic rituals, yajnas, weddings, and other religious ceremonies.
 
• It is also a space for devotees to sing bhajans (devotional songs) and meditate.

questions.question: The largest monolithic rock structure in the world, the Kailasa Temple, is situated in which of the following caves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ellora caves**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Kailasa Temple is located in the **Ellora Caves**, situated in Maharashtra, India.
 
• It is a massive monolithic rock-cut temple dedicated to **Lord Shiva**, built during the reign of the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I in the 8th century CE.
 
• The temple was carved out of a single rock using the **vertical excavation method**, starting at the top and working downward.
 
• The Kailasa Temple is renowned for its intricate carvings, massive size, and architectural brilliance, making it one of the largest monolithic structures in the world.
 
• The Ellora Caves are a UNESCO World Heritage Site, consisting of 34 caves that include Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain monuments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Monolithic Architecture:** Monolithic structures are carved out of a single piece of material, often stone, showcasing advanced engineering and artistic skills.
 
• **Vertical Excavation Method:** This technique involves carving structures from the top down, enabling precision and stability during construction.
 
• **Rashtrakuta Dynasty:** The Rashtrakutas were a prominent dynasty in South India, known for their contributions to art, architecture, and literature.
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Status:** The Ellora Caves were designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983 for their historical, cultural, and architectural significance.
 
• **Ellora Caves Layout:** The caves are divided into three groups: 12 Buddhist caves (1–12), 17 Hindu caves (13–29), and 5 Jain caves (30–34), reflecting India's pluralistic heritage.

questions.question: Which of the following is a National Park in Rajasthan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ranthambore National Park**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ranthambore National Park** is located in the Sawai Madhopur district of Rajasthan, India.
 
• It is one of the largest and most renowned national parks in Northern India.
 
• The park is famous for its significant population of Bengal tigers and provides a unique opportunity for tiger sightings in their natural habitat.
 
• Established in 1980, Ranthambore was declared a National Park under the Wildlife Protection Act.
 
• It is part of the larger Ranthambore Tiger Reserve, which is managed under India's Project Tiger initiative.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Project Tiger:**

 
 
• Launched in 1973, Project Tiger is India's flagship conservation program aimed at preserving Bengal tigers and their habitats.
 
• The initiative involves habitat restoration, anti-poaching measures, and community participation.
 
• Ranthambore National Park is one of the key tiger reserves under this project.
 
 
 
• **Wildlife Protection Act of 1972:**
 
 
• The act provides the legal framework for wildlife conservation and the establishment of National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries in India.
 
• Ranthambore National Park was designated under this act to protect its diverse flora and fauna.
 
 
 
• **Geography of Ranthambore:**
 
 
• The park spans an area of approximately 1,334 square kilometers, including the core and buffer zones.
 
• It features dry deciduous forests, open grasslands, and rocky terrains, making it a unique ecosystem.
 
 
 
• **Key Attractions:**
 
 
• Besides tigers, the park is home to leopards, sambar deer, chital, nilgai, and sloth bears.
 
• Popular landmarks include the Ranthambore Fort, Padam Talao (lake), and ancient banyan trees.

questions.question: Among the following cities, which is closest to the Prime Meridian?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Ahmedabad​**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Prime Meridian is the 0° longitude line that passes through Greenwich, London, and is used as the reference point for global longitude measurements.
 
• Among the cities listed, Ahmedabad is geographically the closest to the Prime Meridian.
 
• Ahmedabad – ~72.6° E is actually closer to 0° longitude.
 
• Ahmedabad (72.6° E) is the closest to the Prime Meridian among the given cities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prime Meridian:** The Prime Meridian is the starting point for measuring longitude and divides the Earth into the Eastern and Western Hemispheres.
 
• **Longitude:** Longitude lines run vertically around the globe and are measured in degrees east or west of the Prime Meridian.
 
• **Geographical Proximity:** When determining proximity to the Prime Meridian, cities with smaller absolute longitudes are closer, regardless of their latitude.
 
• **Indian Cities:** Indian cities like Delhi, Ahmedabad, and Kanyakumari are in the Eastern Hemisphere, with longitudes greater than 0°.
 
• **Significance of the Prime Meridian:** It serves as the basis for Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) and aids in global navigation and timekeeping systems.

questions.question: Which Princely State had a representative assembly from as early as 1881?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mysore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The princely state of **Mysore** was one of the progressive states in British India and introduced a representative assembly as early as **1881**.
 
• The assembly was established under the reign of Maharaja **Chamarajendra Wadiyar X** to provide limited representation to the people.
 
• This was an important step towards constitutional governance and public involvement in administration in princely states.
 
• The Mysore Representative Assembly was one of the **earliest examples of democratic institutions** within a princely state during British rule.
 
• The assembly primarily acted as an advisory body and discussed matters related to the administration of the state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Princely States in British India**:

 
 
• India had over 500 princely states during British rule, which were governed by local rulers but under British suzerainty.
 
• The princely states had varying levels of autonomy in administration and governance.
 
• Mysore was among the most advanced princely states in terms of governance and infrastructure development.
 
 
 
• **Mysore's Progressive Policies**:
 
 
• Mysore is known for its early emphasis on education, industrialization, and public welfare.
 
• The establishment of representative institutions reflected the state's commitment to modernization.
 
 
 
• **Role of Representative Assemblies**:
 
 
• Representative assemblies in princely states acted as consultative bodies, advising rulers on matters of public interest.
 
• They were early experiments in democratic governance, paving the way for modern legislative structures.
 
 
 
• **Chamarajendra Wadiyar X**:
 
 
• He was the ruler of Mysore from 1868 to 1894 and played a key role in modernizing the state.
 
• Under his reign, Mysore saw significant advancements in governance and infrastructure.

questions.question: Which of the following medicines discovered by Paul Ehrlich became the first successful treatment for syphilis?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Salvarsan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Salvarsan**, also known as Arsphenamine, was discovered by Paul Ehrlich in 1909 as the first effective treatment for syphilis.
 
• It was marketed as the "magic bullet" for its ability to target disease-causing pathogens without harming the host.
 
• Salvarsan is an organoarsenic compound, and its discovery marked a significant breakthrough in chemotherapy.
 
• The drug was revolutionary in reducing mortality and morbidity associated with syphilis, which was a major public health issue at the time.
 
• Paul Ehrlich's discovery laid the foundation for modern targeted drug therapy, influencing the development of antibiotics and other treatments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Syphilis:** A sexually transmitted bacterial infection caused by the spirochete Treponema pallidum. It progresses through primary, secondary, latent, and tertiary stages.
 
• **Paul Ehrlich:** A German physician and scientist known for his work in immunology, chemotherapy, and the discovery of Salvarsan.
 
• ** Ehrlich's concept of creating drugs that specifically target pathogens without damaging host cells, which became a cornerstone of pharmacology.
 
• Organometallic Compounds:** Salvarsan was one of the first organometallic compounds used in medicine, showcasing the potential of synthetic chemistry in drug discovery.
 
• **Antibiotics Development:** While Salvarsan was effective, the later discovery of Penicillin in 1928 by Alexander Fleming overshadowed it due to Penicillin's broader spectrum and fewer side effects.
